title: Los Angeles weather: Fire danger rises as Santa Ana winds, heat move into Southern California - ABC7 Los Angeles
text:
Los Angeles weather: Fire danger rises as Santa Ana winds, heat move into Southern California - ABC7 Los Angeles 
 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California Weather 
 Fire danger rises as Santa Ana winds, heat move into SoCal 
 Santa Ana winds, low humidity and hotter temperatures are bringing elevated fire danger to Southern California this weekend. Friday, November 6, 2026 1:36PM Share Follow ABC7 on Google Este artículo se ofrece en Español LOS ANGELES (KABC) -- Santa Ana winds, low humidity and hotter temperatures are bringing elevated fire danger to Southern California this weekend.
 Several parts of Los Angeles County will be under a red flag warning from 2 a.m. to 6 p.m. Saturday. Those areas include the Santa Clarita Valley, Santa Monica Mountains, Santa Susana Mountains and western San Gabriel Mountains, including the Highway 14 corridor.
 The National Weather Service also issued coastal alerts as high tides are expected.
 A beach hazards statement will be in effect through Tuesday morning along the coast of Ventura and L.A. counties. High tides will build each morning and peak Sunday and Monday at 7.2 to 7.6 feet, while a west-to-northwest swell will increase the risk of hazardous swimming conditions, the weather service said.
 The Orange County coast will be under a coastal flood advisory from 4 a.m. to noon Tuesday. The weather service said high tide is expected to peak at 7.4 to 7.6 feet Sunday and Monday. Surf will also increase.
 Friday weather
 Los Angeles and Orange counties can expect a high of 83 degrees with a low of 59 on Friday. Gusty winds start to blow in the canyon passes late Friday. There will be elevated fire danger on Saturday.
 The valleys and the Inland Empire will see a high of 85 degrees and a low of 52 on Friday. Expect stronger winds Friday night, with increased fire risk on Saturday.
 Beach communities can expect sunny conditions on Friday, with a high of 80 degrees and a low of 62.
 Mountain areas will see mostly sunny skies on Friday, with a high of 60 degrees and a low of 30. Expect gusts around 35 mph on Friday and Saturday.
 Deserts are expected to reach a high of 74 degrees and a low of 39 on Friday. Palm Springs is expected to reach a high of 84 degrees.
 City News Service contributed to this report.
